body.p: Claims 1-21 are pending in the application, and claims 16-21 are withdrawn from consideration.
Claims1-15 are rejected.
Claims 1-16, and 18-21 are amended above, and claims 22-27 are newly added. Support is provided by the originally filed specification, claims, and drawings. No new matter has been added.

Applicant reserves the right to reassert any of the claims cancelled or the original or previous claim scope of any claim amended, during the prosecution of this application, in this continuing application.
In view of the above, favorable consideration is respectfully requested.
Please find attached a copy of WO 2011113101 for the Examiner's consideration. This reference does not disclose the claimed subject matter.
Claims 4 and 9-13 are objected to on page 3 of the Office Action. The claims are amended above in response thereto.
Claims 1-15 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. 112(b) or35 U.S.C. 112 (pre-AIA), second paragraph on page 4 of the Office Action. The claims are amended above in response thereto.
A. Claims 1-8 and 11-15 are rejected under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(b) as being
anticipated by Wang et al. ("Wang", US 2011/0302694) on page 7 of the
Office Action.
The Office Action asserts that claims 1-8 and 11-15 are anticipated by Wang.
This rejection is respectfully traversed.

Wang discloses a glove 102 having a flexible sensor 104. The flexible sensor is operationally coupled to a light detector 106, a light source 108, and a second light detector 110. A wrist cuff 112 includes a control panel 114, which may house the operational circuitry and one or more power supplies for the light source 108 and the light detectors 106 and 110. A cable 116 operationally couples the control panel 114 to a data acquisition module 118. The data acquisition module 118 is operationally coupled to a graphical display and control module 120.
It is noted that in Wang, the glove 102 and wrist cuff 112 are separate components, and wrist cuff 112 is not part of the glove, as shown in FIG. 1.

Further, Wang discloses that the "wrist cuff 112 includes circuitry for driving the light source 106, collecting signals from the light detectors 108 and 110, amplifying the signal (amplifier 604), converting analog to digital, indicating conditions on the wrist cuff 112, transmitting the data wirelessly to the control and display unit 620, and housing a rechargeable battery" (see paragraphs [0138] and [0139]).

Wang does not disclose the claimed subject matter, including "a microcontroller secured to the glove." Further, Wang does not disclose the claimed subject matter, including "one or more pressure sensors secured to a side of the glove" (claim 1), or one or more pressure sensors secured to a back of the glove" (claim 26).

In view of the above, it is submitted that Wang does not teach each and every element of the claims as required for anticipation under 35 U.S.C. 102. Thus, the Examiner is respectfully requested to withdraw this rejection.
B. Claims 1-15 are rejected under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(b) as being
anticipated by Montgomery (US 2012/018543) on page 9 of the
Office Action.
The Office Action asserts that claims 1-15 are anticipated by Montgomery.
This rejection is respectfully traversed.
Montgomery discloses a glove device 10 having multiple force sensors 34, a component 36 that is in communication with each of the forces sensors 34, and a motion sensor 40, as shown in FIGS. 1 and 2.

The component 36 comprises a digital signal processor that receives signals from the force sensors 34 and forwards them on to another device, such as a computer. In other embodiments, the component 36 comprises one or more pressure transducers that sense the pressure of the fluid within the forces sensors 34.

Montgomery does not disclose the claimed subject matter, including "one or more pressure sensors secured to a side of the glove" (claim 1), or "one or more pressure sensors secured to a back of the glove" (claim 26).

In view of the above, it is submitted that Montgomery does not teach each and every element of the claims as required for anticipation under 35 U.S.C. 102. Thus, the Examiner is respectfully requested to withdraw this rejection.
A. Claim 9 is rejected under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 103(a) as being unpatentable
over Wang in view of Montgomery on page 12 of the Office Action.

The Office Action asserts that "[I]t would have been obvious to one of ordinary skill in the art at the time of the invention to mount the control panel 114 of Wang between adjacent layers of Montgomery since (1) it can protect the control panel 114 and/or (2) it is simple substitution of one know element for another to obtain predictable results."
Wang and Montgomery are discussed in detail above, which discussions are incorporated herein by reference.

Again, Wang and Montgomery do not disclose the claimed subject matter, including "one or more pressure sensors secured to a side of the glove" (claim 1), or "one or more pressure sensors secured to a back of the glove" (claim 26).
Thus, factually Wang and/or Montgomery cannot teach or suggest the claimed subject matter.

In view of above, nothing in Wang and Montgomery, taken alone or in combination, renders the subject matter of the claims obvious within the meaning of 35 U.S.C. 103. Accordingly, the Examiner is respectfully requested to withdraw this rejection.
B. Claim 10 is rejected under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 103(a) as being unpatentable
over Wang on page 12 of the Office Action.

The Office Action asserts that "[I]t would have been obvious to one of ordinary skill in the art at the time of the invention to substitute the sensors of FIGS. 1-2 and paragraph [0111] of Wang with the sensor FIG. 31 and paragraph [0228] of Wang, since it is a simple substitution of one known element for another to obtain predictable results."
Wang is discussed in detail above, which discussion is incorporated herein by reference.

Again, Wang does not disclose the claimed subject matter, including "one or more pressure sensors secured to a side of the glove" (claim 1), or "one or more pressure sensors secured to a back of the glove" (claim 26).
Thus, factually Wang cannot teach or suggest the claimed subject matter.
In view of above, nothing in Wang renders the subject matter of the claims obvious within the meaning of 35 U.S.C. 103. Accordingly, the Examiner is respectfully requested to withdraw this rejection.
